Ch 9 · Some Applications of Trigonometry — Practice

Attempt first, then open the answer. Everything here is original practice material mapped to the current syllabus.

MCQs

The angle of depression is always measured from: (a) the vertical (b) the horizontal (c) the object (d) the ground below

(b) The horizontal at the observer’s end.

If the angle of elevation of the sun is 45°, the length of the shadow of a pole equals: (a) half its height (b) its height (c) twice its height (d) √3 times its height

(b) Its height. tan 45° = 1.

From the top of a tower the angle of depression of an object on the ground is 30°. The angle of elevation of the top from that object is: (a) 30° (b) 45° (c) 60° (d) 90°

(a) 30°. Alternate angles between parallel horizontals.

Written questions

3 marks The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point 30 m from its foot is 60°. Find the height of the tower.

tan 60° = h/30, so √3 = h/30.
h = 30√3 m ≈ 51.96 m.

3 marks From the top of a 75 m high lighthouse, the angles of depression of two ships on the same side are 30° and 45°. Find the distance between the ships.

For the ship at 45°: tan 45° = 75/x, so x = 75 m.
For the ship at 30°: tan 30° = 75/y, so y = 75√3 m.
Distance = 75√3 − 75 = 75(√3 − 1) ≈ 54.9 m.

4 marks A person on the bank of a river sees the top of a tree on the opposite bank at an angle of elevation of 60°. Walking 20 m away from the bank, the angle becomes 30°. Find the height of the tree and the width of the river.

Let the height be h and the width x.
From the nearer point: h = x√3. From the farther point: h = (x + 20)/√3.
Equating: x√3 = (x + 20)/√3, so 3x = x + 20 and x = 10 m.
Therefore h = 10√3 ≈ 17.32 m and the river is 10 m wide.
